newsitem.title: USA: U.S. holiday company sees expansion in 1997. [CORRECTED 20:00 GMT, 14/10/96].
newsitem.headline: U.S. holiday company sees expansion in 1997. [CORRECTED 20:00 GMT, 14/10/96].

text.p: Interval International sees a timeshare vacation boom ahead and plans to expand aggressively into Asia, its chief executive officer said on Friday.
It is also planning more projects with its prestigious clients Marriott, Hyatt and Disney, Craig Nash told Reuters in an interview.
Miami-based Interval has 700,000 member families and nearly 1,400 member resorts in more than 60 countries. It is wholly-owned by CUC International, which is based in Stamford, Connecticut.
(Corrects number of member families from 7,000).
CUC's revenues for the second quarter increased 19 percent to $490.4 million, as compared with $410 million for the same quarter a year ago.
A breakdown of figures for Interval was not available.
Nash said the timeshare market was the fastest expanding sector of the travel industry and sales could at least double in the next 10 years.
According to the American Resort Development Association, worldwide time-share sales exceeded $5 billion in 1995.
Nash expects Interval's revenue to grow 20 percent over the year.
Income would be less because of expansion costs and software purchases.
Interval does not own or operate the resorts in its network, but offers members the chance to exchange the week they own for another time or place.
"We are a backroom service provider. We are adding more and more services we are offering to our clients," Nash said.
These include flights and car rentals.
"Our goal is to affiliate the highest quality resorts. Part of that includes going after the highest quality vacation operators," Nash said.
"Marriot is continually aquiring locations. They have pretty substantial plans. Hyatt has several projects going on."
Interval is due to begin working with Inter-Continental.
"It's important to note that Marriot and Disney were previously serviced by our main competitor then switched over to us," he said.
Interval is expanding its office in Singapore to develop the Asian market.
"We have made a very large commitment to expansion in Asia. There is great opportunity in these markets," he said.
The company has or is seeking affiliates and projects in Malaysia, the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, China and Japan. The quality of Asian resorts had improved greatly in recent years.

Asia was Interval's greatest growth area, but in numbers Mexico and South America still surpassed it, Nash said. The Caribbean market had suffered in recent years because of a spate of hurricanes and bad storms.
"Before demand exceeded supply. Now people are more reluctant to go there," he said.
Most Americans still preferred to holiday within the United States, with Orlando the most popular destination followed by Las Vegas.
